title: VPC route-matrix Terraform module with endpoint probers
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (route-matrix) that centralizes subnet routing, NAT/IGW assignment, and VPC endpoint wiring for private deployments. The goal is to ship a modules/route-matrix Terraform package that: (1) declares subnet profiles (control, compute, infra) and emits route tables per AZ; (2) manages NAT gateway or Egress NAT instances with controlled failover; (3) creates and maintains gateway (S3) and interface endpoints (ECR, SecretsManager, KMS) with per-environment policies; (4) populates a computed route matrix (subnet -> destination -> next_hop) to make changes auditable and testable; and (5) deploys lightweight endpoint probers (lambda + simple EC2/k8s job) that exercise critical paths and export metrics for alerts. This ticket includes API surface, upgrade strategy, health-check integration, and CI test harness for acceptance testing.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes input variables for subnet profiles, az mapping, nat_mode (managed|self-hosted), endpoint_map, and route_overrides
Applying module in a staging account provisions subnets, route tables, NAT/IGW, and endpoints without manual steps
Route-matrix output is a stable JSON map (list of strings) that can be consumed by console and rollout scripts
Endpoint probers run on a 1m schedule, emit metrics to CloudWatch/Prometheus, and generate PagerDuty alerts on 3 consecutive failures
Upgrade path: 0.x -> 1.0 can be performed with a canary apply in one AZ and no traffic loss for existing flows
Module unit/integration tests run in CI and pass (terraform validate/plan/apply/destroy in ephemeral sandbox)
technical_notes: Design choices: favor declarative computed routing rather than imperative per-route resources so the module surfaces the full intended state (route-matrix) in outputs. Use Terraform 1.6+ with for_each on computed maps to keep drift small. NAT options: managed AWS NAT Gateway for standard use; a self-hosted NAT ASG pattern for cost-sensitive customers with documented tradeoffs. Endpoint policies are templated; we will provide examples for least-privilege patterns for logs/metrics buckets. Health probes: lightweight Lambda in each AZ that performs TCP handshake to interface endpoint ENIs and a small HTTP GET to S3 gateway endpoints; metric namespace redwood/vpc-route-matrix. Use IAM role-per-environment with minimal privileges for probe functions. Avoid creating cross-account resources — prefer module inputs to accept pre-existing IAM roles when needed.
implementation_tasks: Define module inputs/outputs and write README with example usage (private account, dedicated-reserved, staging)
Implement subnet tiling logic and AZ-aware route table generation
Implement NAT selection resource that chooses IGW+NAT or NAT ASG based on nat_mode
Wire gateway and interface endpoints with optional policy templates and endpoint security groups
Compute route-matrix output and add a terraform local to render it as JSON
Create endpoint prober Lambda with Terraform resource and CloudWatch metric alarms
Add CI job: terraform validate -> plan (diff) -> apply in ephemeral sandbox -> run smoke probes -> destroy
Add example overlay for Private deployment (VPC peering/VPN) with route overrides
Docs: upgrade notes, canary apply steps, and runbook for routing regressions
test_plan: Unit tests: terraform fmt/validate for all module files
Integration: create ephemeral VPC in CI runner, apply module with nat_mode=managed, run probers, assert CloudWatch metrics show success
Chaos test: simulate NAT gateway deletion and verify module auto-heals or alerts and that traffic from compute subnets fails over according to policy
Compatibility: verify module works with existing remote state backends used by private deployments
Security: static scan of endpoint policies, ensure no overly permissive wildcard principals
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy module to internal staging account with single AZ canary and monitor metrics for 24h
Stage 2: Deploy to customer-like sandbox with multi-AZ and synthetic traffic for 48h
Stage 3: Enable module for one small production VPC behind a feature flag with gradual rollout across AZs
Rollback: run terraform apply with previous pinned module version and traffic will follow existing route tables; runbook includes steps to re-associate route tables and re-create NAT if needed
